name: Veldtmark AirMesh UV Field Shirt
description: Loose-cut shirt in UPF-60 open-weave synth-linen, pale bone with faded indigo sleeve panels. Moisture-wicking inner layer pulls sweat away from chrome ports, with reinforced shoulder channels for spinal rig clearance. Vented back yoke lets lake wind through without flapping.
functionality: UPF-60 sun protection, chrome-port venting channels, moisture-wicking inner layer, aug-compatible shoulder seams.
what_it_says: You dress practically and know what a Great Lakes summer actually does to a body.
story_hooks: The shirt's port channel is slightly too wide — custom-cut for someone else's spinal rig model.
Someone stenciled a union glyph inside the collar, hidden unless you look.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A relaxed, deliberately oversized shirt with an understated utilitarian aesthetic. The pale bone base contrasts sharply with faded indigo sleeve panels that suggest wear or intentional fading. The silhouette is loose enough to accommodate cybernetic augmentation without constraint, with a subtle drape that moves with body mechanics rather than against them.
physical_description.fit: Loose and intentionally spacious through the torso and shoulders, with strategic reinforcement around the shoulder blades and spinal column. The cut allows for hidden tech integration and augmentation clearance without appearing baggy—a calculated ergonomic design.
physical_description.primary_material: UPF-60 open-weave synth-linen composite with moisture-wicking inner layer. The weave is deliberately porous, designed for rapid evaporative cooling in high-humidity Great Lakes environments.
physical_description.texture: The outer surface has a slightly crisp, linen-like hand with visible weave texture. The open mesh structure creates subtle shadow play across the fabric. The inner layer is smooth and silky, engineered to slide against skin without friction against chrome or subcutaneous ports.
physical_description.color_scheme: Pale bone (off-white) as primary, with faded indigo sleeve panels that show uneven color saturation—either from sun exposure or intentional acid washing. No visible branding or loud accents; the color palette reads as deliberately muted and professional.
physical_description.closures: Likely magnetic snap closures or friction-fit placket down the front—no traditional buttons that would snag on augmentation rigs. Side seams may feature concealed zippers for venting.
distinctive_features: Reinforced shoulder channels cut to accommodate spinal interface rigs
Vented back yoke with engineered apertures for air circulation without flapping
Moisture-wicking inner layer with chrome port compatibility
Open-weave construction optimized for lakeside wind patterns
Faded indigo panels suggesting either genuine wear or intentional aesthetic aging
Hidden pocket construction for tech integration
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 transition. Premium materials and thoughtful engineering signal corpo-adjacent functionality, but the practical aesthetic and lack of ostentatious branding keep it accessible to skilled working-class operators.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by augmented field workers, industrial medics, chrome-rig pilots, and corpo field teams operating in the humid industrial zones around Lake Michigan. The design says 'I have investment in my body—both biological and synthetic—and I respect the environment I work in.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually broken-in but meticulously maintained. The indigo panels show natural fading from sun and salt spray exposure. Worn but not distressed; any tears would be immediately repaired. The fabric develops a subtle patina over time without deteriorating.
